assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks have transformed precision measurement, reached remarkable performance, and enable new tests of fundamental physics.
assessment.attribution: Katori introduced the magic-wavelength lattice-clock concept; Ye made decisive experimental advances and broad metrological demonstrations.
assessment.maturity: The technology is extensively reproduced, operationally reliable, and approaching deployment in international time standards.
uncertainties: The eventual extent of routine redefinition or replacement of present primary time standards remains unsettled.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Atom interferometry created an exceptionally sensitive measurement platform for gravity, inertial sensing, and fundamental tests.
assessment.attribution: Bordé provided foundational light-pulse interferometer concepts, while Kasevich and Pritchard drove defining precision-measurement implementations.
assessment.maturity: Its central effects and methods are long established, with broad experimental replication and increasingly capable instruments.
uncertainties: The most consequential applications, especially field-deployed quantum sensors, are still developing.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical coherence tomography opened a noninvasive, high-resolution way to image living tissue and has had exceptional scientific and medical impact.
assessment.attribution: Huang, Swanson, and Fujimoto are closely associated with the seminal demonstration and the essential instrumentation.
assessment.maturity: The technique is mature, independently replicated, and an established clinical and research instrument.
uncertainties: Credit allocation among foundational interferometric imaging, early system development, and later clinical translation requires careful archival assessment.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: High-gain X-ray free-electron lasers have supplied a qualitatively new ultrafast and coherent probe of matter.
assessment.attribution: Pellegrini and Kim were central to the physical and accelerator concepts, and Rossbach to the realization of a working high-gain X-ray FEL.
assessment.maturity: Major facilities have reliably delivered the capability for years, enabling a wide experimental community.
uncertainties: The balance of credit between theoretical proposals, accelerator development, and facility realization is intrinsically broad.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Trapped ions remain a leading, high-fidelity architecture for quantum computation and precise quantum simulation.
assessment.attribution: Cirac and Zoller supplied seminal schemes, while Blatt delivered pioneering and sustained experimental realization.
assessment.maturity: Core operations, entanglement, and programmable simulations are repeatedly demonstrated with strong control and verification.
uncertainties: The field has many indispensable contributors, making a three-person attribution necessarily selective.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical control of individual defect spins made a powerful bridge between solid-state quantum physics and nanoscale sensing.
assessment.attribution: Awschalom helped establish semiconductor spin control; Wrachtrup and Walsworth made defining contributions to single-defect sensing and applications.
assessment.maturity: Single-spin control and quantum sensing are well reproduced and now support active research and instrument development.
uncertainties: Mikhail D. Lukin and other contributors also have substantial claims to foundational credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Cavity optomechanics enabled measurement and quantum control of mechanical motion at previously inaccessible limits.
assessment.attribution: Aspelmeyer, Painter, and Kippenberg each made central experimental and conceptual contributions to the modern field.
assessment.maturity: Quantum-limited measurement, cooling, and coherent optomechanical control have been demonstrated by many laboratories.
uncertainties: Whether the field's ultimate impact will rest primarily in fundamental tests, transduction, or sensing is still unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultracold atoms in optical lattices became an extraordinarily clean and controllable platform for many-body quantum physics.
assessment.attribution: Bloch, Greiner, and Esslinger led landmark experimental demonstrations that established the platform's capabilities.
assessment.maturity: The methods are robust and widely used, with long-standing experimental confirmation of major lattice-model phenomena.
uncertainties: Juan Ignacio Cirac and Peter Zoller have major theoretical claims, and the credit set exceeds three people.
